title: Testing (pytest + httpx)
summary: TestClient, database-per-test fixtures, dependency overrides, and testing authenticated endpoints.

sections.content: TestClient wraps httpx and runs your app in-process — no server needed. It supports async routes via anyio.

import pytest
from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool

TEST_URL = "sqlite://"
engine = create_engine(TEST_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False},
                       poolclass=StaticPool)
TestingSession = sessionmaker(bind=engine, autocommit=False, autoflush=False)

@pytest.fixture()
def db_session():
    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
    session = TestingSession()
    yield session
    session.close()
    Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)

@pytest.fixture()
def client(db_session):
    def override_get_db():
        yield db_session
    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        yield c
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()

sections.title: StaticPool
sections.content: Use StaticPool so the in-memory SQLite DB is shared between sessions — each session sees the same in-memory database.

def test_protected(client):
    # No token → 401
    r = client.get("/users/me")
    assert r.status_code == 401

    # Login and use token
    token = client.post("/login", data={"username": "u", "password": "p"}).json()["access_token"]
    r = client.get("/users/me", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    assert r.status_code == 200

code_challenge.title: Test Your First Endpoint
code_challenge.description: Create a FastAPI app with GET / that returns {"message": "Hello"}. Write a TestClient test that asserts the response.
code_challenge.starter_code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def read_root():
    return {"message": "Hello"}

client = TestClient(app)

# TODO: Write a test function that:
# 1. Calls client.get('/')
# 2. Asserts status_code == 200
# 3. Asserts json() == {"message": "Hello"}
# Print the result

# Run the test
client = TestClient(app)
r = client.get("/")
print("Status:", r.status_code)
print("Body:", r.json())
assert r.status_code == 200
assert r.json() == {"message": "Hello"}
print("Test passed!")

quiz.question: What does TestClient do?
options: Wraps httpx to run your app in-process (no server needed)
quiz.explanation: TestClient uses httpx with ASGITransport to run your FastAPI app in-process. No server, no port, no network — just direct ASGI calls.

quiz.question: How do you override a dependency for testing?
quiz.explanation: app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db swaps the dependency for tests. Clear it with app.dependency_overrides.clear() after.

quiz.question: Why use StaticPool for in-memory SQLite tests?
options: Shares the in-memory DB across sessions so tests see the same data
quiz.explanation: StaticPool keeps a single connection alive, so all sessions share the same in-memory SQLite database. Without it, each session gets its own empty DB.

quiz.question: How do you test an endpoint that requires authentication?
options: Override get_current_user to return a test user, or login and use the token
quiz.explanation: Either override get_current_user in dependency_overrides (simpler) or POST to /login with test credentials and pass the Bearer token in headers (more realistic).

quiz.question: What should you do after tests that use dependency_overrides?
quiz.explanation: Always clear dependency_overrides after tests to prevent leaks between test cases. The fixture pattern with yield + clear is the standard approach.
